prompt:
Scene:
A square-format 90s consumer snapshot of a drained hotel-basement swimming pool at night, taken with direct on-camera flash. The flash is the only light in the room. The basin is completely dry and scraped back to pale concrete. Deep green-and-cream ceramic tile lines the walls, with a painted black stripe at the old waterline. Slight magenta color cast and visible film grain.

Subject:
A rectangular three-lane basement pool viewed from a raised deck corner, slightly above the rim. The bottom is dry, with a single circular drain cover at the lowest point and a small puddle around it. Two tile wall steps on the far end descend into the basin. A metal handrail runs along the near deck. The tiled walls reflect the flash as small specular hits, and the air feels enclosed and humid.

Important details:
Hard flash falloff is essential. Tile geometry must be crisp and regular. The absence of water must be unambiguous — viewer sees the basin bottom clearly. The feeling should be 'nobody has been down here for months'. No swimmers, no staff, no towels. Tile color palette: pale ivory deck, chlorine-faded green wall, warmer ceramic underfoot.

Use case:
Empty Pool single study 1/5, wide view of a drained basement basin.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio, no people, no reflection of photographer, no cinematic color grade, no dramatic fog.
